To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
inhibition of the PI3K/mTor-pathway in ovarian cancer cells leads to adaptive resistance, which is mediated by drug induced upregulation of BCL-2, EGFP, and IGFR1.
Inhibition of PI3 kinase/mTOR (PI3K/mTOR) in ovarian cancer-spheres leads to death of matrix-deprived inner cells, whereas matrix-associated outer cells are resistant.
dual inhibition of the PI3K/m-TOR pathway in ovarian cancer cells leads to adaptive resistance that can be bypassed by targeting the upregulated survival programs in the resistant cancer cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of cancer cell adaptation to targeted therapies and how this knowledge can be applied to improve drug efficacy.
the development of a novel strategy for the treatment of ovarian cancer, which is based on the combination of PI3K inhibitors with drugs that target the upregulated proteins.
the mechanisms of resistance to targeted therapies, in particular to PI3K inhibitors in cancer cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PI3K/mTor pathway is a major target for ovarian cancer therapy, however, resistance can be overcome by combining PI3K/mTOr inhibition with inhibitors of other survival pathways.

PI3K/mTORM-targeted therapy in ovarian cancer cells leads to adaptive resistance, which is mediated through drug-induced upregulations of survival programs, and that bypassing this resistance mechanism could improve PI3K/mTor-targeted drug efficacy in ovarian cancers.
Inhibition of the PI3K/mTor pathway in ovarian cancer-spheres leads to death of cells in the interior of the sphere, whereas cells attached to the matrix are resistant.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PI3K/mTor pathway is a major driver of cancer cell survival.
the PI3K/mTor pathway is the most commonly mutated pathway in epithelial cancer, and that it is a very attractive target for cancer therapeutical.
PI3K/mTor inhibition leads to adaptive resistance and that this resistance is mediated by the activation of survival pathways.
The main takeaway from our work is that
matrix-associated resistance to PI3KI/mTORI is a consequence of the upregulation of a set of survival proteins that are normally induced upon nutrient or growth factor starvation.
PI3K/mTor inhibition in ovarian cancer cells induces a stress response that is associated with resistance.
PI3K inhibition can be used as a tool to identify and target resistance mechanisms in epithelial tumors.
